original_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob, and let X = product_i Xi be a product of T0 spaces. If each Ai subset Xi is K-determined, must the product subset product_i Ai also be K-determined?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official open problem almost verbatim: it has the right ambient category K, the product space X=∏_{i∈I}X_i of T0 spaces, the hypotheses A_i⊆X_i are K-determined, and the exact conclusion asked is whether ∏_{i∈I}A_i must be K-determined. The nearby context also shows this is the subset-level product question, not the broader space-level Question 5.21. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
missing_details: The draft does not define what “K-determined” means: for a subset A of a T0 space X, every continuous map f:X→Y into any K-space Y must send A to a singleton {y_A}, with y_A unique. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

It should specify that {X_i : i∈I} is an arbitrary indexed family of T0 spaces and X=∏_{i∈I}X_i; the question is not restricted to finite products. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

It should say explicitly that the product set ∏_{i∈I}A_i is being viewed as a subset of the product space X, and its K-determinedness is tested against continuous maps defined on X, not on the individual factors. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The universal quantifiers should be explicit: for every i∈I, A_i⊆X_i is K-determined, and the conclusion asks whether for every K-space Y and every continuous f:X→Y, f(∏_{i∈I}A_i) is a singleton. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

To stay paper-faithful, one should not add extra hypotheses such as closedness, irreducibility, saturatedness, or finite index set; none of these appear in Question 5.20. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

If desired, the parenthetical scope note from the paper can be retained: K is any full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob, with Keimel-Lawson categories as a prominent special case. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
refined_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 with Sob⊆K (for example, a Keimel-Lawson category), let X=∏_{i∈I}X_i be the product of an arbitrary family {X_i:i∈I} of T0 spaces, and suppose that for each i∈I the subset A_i⊆X_i is K-determined in the sense that for every continuous map g_i:X_i→Y into any K-space Y, there exists a unique y_i∈Y with g_i(A_i)={y_i}. Must the product subset ∏_{i∈I}A_i be K-determined as a subset of X; equivalently, for every K-space Y and every continuous map f:X→Y, must f(∏_{i∈I}A_i) be a singleton? ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
justification: The draft is targeting the official open problem stated as Question 5.20, not the broader Question 5.21 about products of K-determined spaces. Definition 5.5 supplies the missing stand-alone definition of a K-determined subset, while Section 2 fixes the ambient meaning of K as a full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob and introduces Keimel-Lawson categories. The placement of Question 5.20 immediately after Lemma 5.15 and Theorem 5.16 (arbitrary-product permanence for Rudin sets/spaces) and Lemma 5.17 and Corollary 5.19 (finite-product permanence for WD sets/spaces) shows that the sharp paper-faithful formulation is exactly this subset-level arbitrary-product question, with no extra closedness or irreducibility assumptions. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
